findings.name: Queue pool settings accept a negative "Max Number of workers" and save it
findings.summary: The page shows the green \"Settings Updated\" banner, the queue table now shows \"Max Number of Workers\" = -1 (I typed -5, it stored -1) and the field placeholder reads \"Currently -1\". A negative worker count is persisted in the instance configuration. (on /-/admin/monitor/queue/1)
findings.expected: The page refuses a negative worker count (the same way it refuses letters with \"Max number of workers must be a number\") and keeps the previous value.
findings.actual: The page shows the green \"Settings Updated\" banner, the queue table now shows \"Max Number of Workers\" = -1 (I typed -5, it stored -1) and the field placeholder reads \"Currently -1\". A negative worker count is persisted in the instance configuration.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open Site Administration > Monitoring > Queues (/-/admin/monitor/queue).
Click "Review / Add Workers" on the notification-service row (/-/admin/monitor/queue/1).
In the "Pool Settings" panel, type -5 into the "Max Number of workers" field.
Click "Update Settings".

findings.name: User search treats % and _ as SQL wildcards instead of literal characters
findings.summary: The search term is passed into a SQL LIKE pattern unescaped: '%' matches every user (Total: 3, all rows) and '_lex' matches 'alex' (Total: 1) because _ stands for any single character. A literal search proves it returns records that do not contain the typed text. (on /-/admin/users)
findings.expected: The search box searches usernames literally: no username contains a % or a _ character, so both searches should show 'Total: 0' with 'No results found.'
findings.actual: The search term is passed into a SQL LIKE pattern unescaped: '%' matches every user (Total: 3, all rows) and '_lex' matches 'alex' (Total: 1) because _ stands for any single character. A literal search proves it returns records that do not contain the typed text.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open /-/admin/users (User Account Management (Total: 3), rows: alex, eval, maya).
Type % into the 'Search users...' box and press Enter.
Observe: heading says 'User Account Management (Total: 3)' and all three users are listed.
Now type _lex into the same box and press Enter.
Observe: 'Total: 1' and the single row is alex.

findings.name: Stacktrace page shows only the goroutine count and an empty panel, with no trace or message
findings.summary: Only the header \"142 Goroutines\" (68, then 142 on a second load) is rendered; underneath it the panel is completely blank — no stack text, no placeholder, no error, no message. Reloading and waiting several seconds changes nothing; opening /-/admin/monitor/stacktrace?show=process or ?show=stacktrace shows the full lists, so only the page's default address is empty. (on /-/admin/monitor/stacktrace)
findings.expected: The Stacktrace page shows the goroutine stack trace (or a clear message that no trace is available), the way the Running Processes / Stacktrace tabs show their lists. A header announcing N goroutines should be followed by the traces or an explanation.
findings.actual: Only the header \"142 Goroutines\" (68, then 142 on a second load) is rendered; underneath it the panel is completely blank — no stack text, no placeholder, no error, no message. Reloading and waiting several seconds changes nothing; opening /-/admin/monitor/stacktrace?show=process or ?show=stacktrace shows the full lists, so only the page's default address is empty.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open Site Administration.
Click Monitoring in the left admin menu, then Trace (or open /-/admin/monitor/stacktrace by address).

Look at the content area under the tab bar "Running Processes | Stacktrace": the only thing shown is a header such as "142 Goroutines" with no stack text, no code lines, no empty-state message below it.

findings.name: Unknown queue id gives a completely blank page instead of the site's 404 page
findings.summary: A completely blank white page: no title, no navigation bar, no footer, no text and no link back. The answer is HTTP 404 with an empty body. I saw this for both /-/admin/monitor/queue/999 and /-/admin/monitor/queue/abc. A non-existent address elsewhere on the site (/this-page-does-not-exist-agent9) does render the normal \"404 Not Found - The page you are trying to reach either does not exist or you are not authorized to view it.\" page, so the queue detail route is the odd one out. (on /-/admin/monitor/queue/999)
findings.expected: The normal \"404 Not Found\" page of the site, with the navigation bar and the message that the page does not exist.
findings.actual: A completely blank white page: no title, no navigation bar, no footer, no text and no link back. The answer is HTTP 404 with an empty body. I saw this for both /-/admin/monitor/queue/999 and /-/admin/monitor/queue/abc. A non-existent address elsewhere on the site (/this-page-does-not-exist-agent9) does render the normal \"404 Not Found - The page you are trying to reach either does not exist or you are not authorized to view it.\" page, so the queue detail route is the odd one out.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1.
Open Site Administration > Monitoring > Queues (/-/admin/monitor/queue).
Change the address to a queue id that does not exist: /-/admin/monitor/queue/999 (same with /-/admin/monitor/queue/abc) and press Enter.

findings.name: At tablet and phone widths the \"Download diagnosis report\" button overlaps the \"Stacktrace\" tab
findings.summary: The \"Download diagnosis report\" button sits on top of the \"Stacktrace\" tab: at 768px wide the button covers the right half of the word \"Stacktrace\" (only \"Stac\" is readable) and the \"seconds\" label wraps out of the form under the button, onto the divider; at 390px wide the button covers the tab's right part and the seconds input overlaps the tab row. The tab is declared partly covered by the button, so it can only be clicked on its left part. (on /-/admin/monitor/perftrace and /-/admin/monitor/stacktrace)
findings.expected: The tab bar (Running Processes / Stacktrace) and the "Download diagnosis report  [10] seconds" form each keep their own row at tablet and phone widths: no element covers another, the tab labels stay fully readable and clickable, and "seconds" stays next to its input.
findings.actual: The \"Download diagnosis report\" button sits on top of the \"Stacktrace\" tab: at 768px wide the button covers the right half of the word \"Stacktrace\" (only \"Stac\" is readable) and the \"seconds\" label wraps out of the form under the button, onto the divider; at 390px wide the button covers the tab's right part and the seconds input overlaps the tab row. The tab is declared partly covered by the button, so it can only be clicked on its left part.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open /-/admin/monitor/perftrace (or /-/admin/monitor/stacktrace).
Set the browser window to 768 x 1024: the blue "Download diagnosis report" button overlaps the "Stacktrace" tab in the tab bar, and the word "seconds" falls below the input onto the divider line.
Set the window to 390 x 844: the button still overlaps the "Stacktrace" tab and the "10" seconds input overlaps the tab row.

findings.actual: The Summary shows \"Release 1\" while the instance has no release anywhere: harbor-handbook's Releases tab says \"0 Releases\" (RSS feed empty, no release in the repository sidebar, tag v1.0.0 still offers \"New Release\") and the other two repositories are empty. findings.name: An \"Open with\" editor line without \"=\" is silently dropped on Save, with no error message
findings.summary: The page reloads silently: the textarea comes back containing only "agent2 Editor = agent2://open?url={url}". The line without "=" is discarded without any error or warning next to the field, and no confirmation of any kind is shown for the save. With only the malformed line entered, Save empties the whole field (screenshot s5) and the person is never told their entry was dropped. Repeating the same save gives the same result every time. (on /-/admin/config/settings)
findings.expected: The form should either refuse the line with a message next to the field (e.g. "line 2 has no '=': expected Name = url-with-{url}") and keep what the person typed, or keep the entry as typed. Either way the person must be able to see that their line was not accepted.
findings.actual: The page reloads silently: the textarea comes back containing only "agent2 Editor = agent2://open?url={url}". The line without "=" is discarded without any error or warning next to the field, and no confirmation of any kind is shown for the save. With only the malformed line entered, Save empties the whole field (screenshot s5) and the person is never told their entry was dropped. Repeating the same save gives the same result every time.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open /-/admin/config/settings (Configuration → Settings in the admin sidebar).

In the "Repository" card, put the cursor in the large empty textarea under "The 'Open with' editors for the clone menu…" and type two lines: agent2 Editor = agent2://open?url={url} agent2 Broken Line Without Equals
Click the blue Save button in the same card.
Read the textarea again (reload the page if you like: the stored value is the same).

Only a reload then falls back to the Sign In page. (on /-/admin/users)
findings.expected: After signing out, Back must not show the admin page again: it should go to the sign-in page or an error, because the session no longer exists (reloading the page there does redirect to Sign In, so the access check itself works).
findings.actual: Back shows the full cached admin Users page — "User Account Management (Total: 3)", alex@example.test, admin@example.test, maya@example.test, the Admin Settings sidebar and the eval avatar in the navbar — to a visitor who is signed out. Only a reload then falls back to the Sign In page.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open /-/admin/users (User Account Management, lists alex, eval, maya with their email addresses).
Open the account menu at the top right and click Sign Out (you land on the signed-out start page).

findings.name: Choosing a filter silently resets the chosen sort order on the admin User Accounts list
findings.summary: The chosen sort is dropped: the address becomes /-/admin/users?q=&status_filter%5Bis_admin%5D=0 (no sort parameter), the rows come back in the default ID-ascending order (alex, maya) and the arrow moves back to ID ▲. Seen 3 times out of 3 tries; the typed search text (q) is kept, only the sort is lost. (on /-/admin/users)
findings.expected: The filter is added on top of the current state: the address keeps sort=reversealphabetically next to the status filter, and the list stays in reverse-alphabetical order (maya, alex) with the ▼ arrow still on Username.
findings.actual: The chosen sort is dropped: the address becomes /-/admin/users?q=&status_filter%5Bis_admin%5D=0 (no sort parameter), the rows come back in the default ID-ascending order (alex, maya) and the arrow moves back to ID ▲. The same happens with other combinations: sort \"Alphabetically\" + filter \"Active\" (address /-/admin/users?q=a&status_filter%5Bis_active%5D=1, alex/eval/maya revert to ID order), sort \"Reverse alphabetically\" + filter \"Admin\". Seen 3 times out of 3 tries; the typed search text (q) is kept, only the sort is lost.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval (password given for the test) and open /-/admin/users.

Open the "Sort" dropdown in the list toolbar and choose "Reverse alphabetically": rows become maya (3), eval (1), alex (2) with a ▼ arrow on the Username column and the address becomes /-/admin/users?q=&sort=reversealphabetically.
Open the "Filter" dropdown and choose "Not Admin".
Read the address and the row order/arrow after the list reloads.

findings.name: A nonexistent admin user address silently shows the user list instead of the site's Not Found page
findings.summary: The address is silently redirected to /-/admin/users and the whole user list is shown, with no error, no message and no sign that the account does not exist.
